title: eval-harness: per-prompt regression checks + quality gating CI hook
author: Maya Patel
description:
Adds a per-prompt regression gating mechanism to the eval-harness and wires it into CI as an optional quality gating hook. Motivation: we frequently ship model and prompt changes that affect specific prompt families; team-level metrics (e.g. aggregate accuracy) can hide prompt-specific regressions. This PR implements per-prompt scoring, configurable thresholds, and a lightweight GitHub Actions CI hook that can block merges when a PR causes regressions beyond tolerated deltas.

What this change includes: - per_prompt_gate: library to compute prompt-set deltas vs. a baseline (supports absolute and relative thresholds) - a canonical eval-config entry for prompt groups and tolerances (eval-configs/prompt-groups.yaml) - a GitHub Actions hook (ci/per-prompt-quality-gate.yml) that runs a fast subset eval on PRs and publishes a JSON report - an opt-in feature flag (ENG feature gate) for repositories to adopt the hook - unit + integration tests and docs describing configuration and rollout.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked (Linear ENG-4521) - [x] Unit tests for gating logic - [x] Integration test exercising action with mock eval outputs - [x] Docs & examples added - [x] Feature gated and opt-in by default

Design notes: The gating logic groups prompts into named sets (e.g. "billing-intent", "ner-edge-cases") and computes aggregated metrics (accuracy, F1, BLEU where applicable). For each prompt-set we compute baseline_score and pr_score; delta = pr_score - baseline_score. A prompt-set fails if delta < threshold (thresholds can be absolute negative deltas or relative percent drops). The CI action runs a fast evaluator (configured per-repo) that executes only the tagged prompt-sets referenced in the PR metadata. Results are uploaded as a JSON artifact and a comment summary is posted on the PR.

Compatibility & rollout: Hook is opt-in; no changes to default CI behavior. Repos can adopt by adding the action and configuring eval-configs/prompt-groups.yaml. The eval-harness will continue to support aggregate gating separately. Backwards-compatible: old configs ignored unless new keys present.

Testing and validation: Ran unit tests (new test_per_prompt_gate.py), ran an end-to-end test in perf-canary against a small model bundle to validate stability, and executed the action on a staging branch with recorded baseline outputs to validate false-positive rates.

Follow-ups: - Dashboard integration (ENG-4590) to show per-prompt trendlines over time - Automatic suggestion tooling to help choose thresholds based on historical variance

References: Linear: ENG-4521, ENG-4590. Related PRs: perf-canary and eval-harness metrics hook work (see linked PRs in repo).

release_notes:
- Added per-prompt regression gating library and GitHub Action for optional CI quality gating.
- Config: eval-configs/prompt-groups.yaml to declare prompt sets and thresholds.
- Opt-in action ci/per-prompt-quality-gate.yml; default sample size configured to reduce PR runtime.
- Docs: eval-harness/docs/quality-gating.md contains setup and best practices.
notes: This PR is intentionally conservative: gating is opt-in and sample-size/timeboxed to avoid slowing developer flow. We observed a handful of historical regressions that would have been caught by per-prompt checks (not by aggregate metrics). Teams adopting this should tune thresholds and sample sizes.
